classification.difficultyReason: Devise an unscaffolded dividing line by reframing half the figure as a whole square plus a triangle, determine the required endpoint from its area, and prove the resulting partition is equal.

content.prompt:
Draw a line through $P$ that splits the 5 squares below into equal areas.

Prove that your answer is correct.

spec.description: Three bottom squares with two more stacked above the central square. All internal boundaries remain visible. This labelled composite arrangement cannot be expressed by the rectangular blank-grid template.
spec.mathematics: Five congruent squares; P is the lower-left corner of the leftmost bottom square.
spec.answerVisibility: No dividing line or answer labels appear in the question figure.

answer.short:
Draw $PX$, where $X$ is the midpoint of the right side of the middle square in the vertical column.

The region below the line is a triangle of area $1.5$ square units plus one square, giving $2.5$ of the five square units.
answer.worked:
Let each square have side length $s$. Label the bottom-right corner of the central bottom square $Q$. On the same vertical edge, let $B$ be one square above $Q$ and $A$ two squares above $Q$. Choose $X$ halfway between $A$ and $B$, and draw $PX$.

$$\begin{align*}PQ&=2s\\QX&=\frac32s\\\text{Area of triangle }PQX&=\frac12\times2s\times\frac32s\\\text{Area of triangle }PQX&=\frac32s^2\\\text{Area below }PX&=\frac32s^2+s^2\\\text{Area below }PX&=\frac52s^2\\\text{Area of all five squares}&=5s^2\end{align*}$$

The triangle and the rightmost bottom square form the region below the line. Its area is half the total, so the line divides the figure into equal areas.
